# Plan: overnight SPE rounds, starting at round 5

I will run SPE rounds back to back while you sleep. Each round goes through specify, predict, evaluate, and learn. I will make a local commit after each step and tag each round when it closes. I will not push, open a PR, deploy, or send any message. I will stop on the rules below and write you a morning report.

I have not loaded the round 4 numbers into this plan. Every number in the round 5 tables comes from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` and the round 4 section of `spe/prediction-log.md`. I will write those numbers into `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` before the predict commit and before any trial runs.

## 1. Caps (please confirm or change before you go)

You did not set a round cap or a budget cap. I propose these. If you approve the plan without changes, these apply.

| Cap | Proposed value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds | At most 4 rounds tonight (r05 to r08) | Each round needs evidence from the last one. More than 4 unreviewed respecs can drift from what you want. |
| Spend per round | At most 1.5x the r04 measured cost | A round that costs much more than r04 means the design changed more than a respec should change it. |
| Spend for the night | At most 4x the r04 measured cost | This is 4 rounds at roughly r04 cost. |
| Clock | No new round starts after 06:00 local time | You get a finished report, not a half-run round. |

## 2. Stop rules

I stop and write the morning report when any of these happens.

1. Predictions hit within their stated error for 3 rounds in a row. I will count back from r04 in the prediction log, so r03 and r04 count if both were hits. If so, I report that the design looks stable enough to judge for go-live.
2. Any cap in section 1 is reached.
3. A failure needs a decision only you can make. Section 3 lists those.
4. Two rounds in a row where every configuration passes everything. One such round leads me to propose harder tasks or stricter graders. A second one means I cannot make the test hard enough without your input.

I halt a round in the middle and report when any of these happens.

- A budget cap is hit during the run.
- An answer key leaks to a trial.
- A grader is found broken during the run.

A halted round still gets a learn commit. That commit records the halt, the partial numbers, and a failure entry. I do not start another round after a halt.

## 3. What I change on my own, and what I leave for you

| I may do this on my own | I leave this for you |
|---|---|
| Add harder tasks when a round measured nothing | Change or drop any requirement whose source is your own words |
| Tighten a grader, with a failure ID as the source | Change the scope of the design under test |
| Fix harness bugs, logged as failure entries | Switch to a model or setting that raises cost per task |
| Change trial counts inside the budget cap | Drop a configuration from the comparison |
| Regrade a round after a grader fix, with the original numbers kept next to the new ones | Anything that leaves this machine |

The author does not touch the judge. Graders are frozen once a round's predict commit lands. A grader change goes into the next round's spec as a requirement with a failure ID as its source.

## 4. Round 5

### Specify

The sources are the "Proposed for round 5" table at the end of the spec and the open entries in `spe/failures.md`.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-n | One row per accepted r04 proposal | The proposal ID and the round 4 evidence it cites | The grader check that measures it |
| R5-f | One row per open failure that the round fixes | The failure ID (F-number) | The check that would have caught it |

Requirements from earlier rounds carry forward unchanged unless a proposal changes them. I write `spe/spec/spec.md` and save the source text under `spe/spec/transcripts/`. Your message tonight is the transcript for this loop.

Commit: `SPE r05 specify: <the changes from r04>`

### Predict

| Metric | Config | Same as last round (r04 measured) | Predicted r05 | Stated error | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pass rate | Each config | From r04 log | A number | A number | The pass check | One line per row |
| Tool calls per task | Each config | From r04 log | A number | A number | The trace counter | One line per row |
| Cost per task | Each config | From r04 log | A number | A number | The cost tally | One line per row |

Every cell is a number when it is committed. Each row names the grader check that measures it. Each Why states one assumption that could turn out wrong. I save `spe/plans/r05.md` and `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`. After the commit I do not edit the predictions.

Commit: `SPE r05 predict: <headline predicted numbers>`

### Evaluate

| Step | Gate |
|---|---|
| 1. Build `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` from r04 plus the spec changes | The script parses and loads with no errors |
| 2. Self-test each grader on one known-pass and one known-fail fixture | Each grader scores both fixtures correctly |
| 3. Check that trials cannot see answer keys | A search of trial inputs and sandbox paths finds no answer key content |
| 4. Dry run with 1 trial per config | The run is clean end to end, and cost per trial is recorded |
| 5. Project the full run cost from the dry run | The projection is under the round cap |

Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (harness): <gates passed>`

I launch one Workflow run with the r04 trial counts, adjusted only by the spec. The cost and time estimate is unmeasured. It is based on r04 actuals and the dry run. The Workflow returns at launch, so I wait for its completion notice before grading. Results go to `spe/evals/results/r05/`.

Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline measured numbers>`

### Close-out (learn)

1. I add the r05 section to `spe/prediction-log.md` with the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. I add "Which Why broke" under the table. If the naive guess beat the predictions, I say so plainly.
2. I add new failure types to `spe/failures.md`, continuing the F-numbers.
3. I add a "Proposed for round 6" table to the spec.
4. I write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`, starting from the r05 measured values.
5. I update `spe/README.md` with the round result and the rerun command.

Commit: `SPE r05 learn: <verdict summary>`, then tag `spe-r05`.

## 5. Rounds 6 and later

Each later round has the same shape as round 5. Before each new round starts, I check every rule in section 2. Each respec uses only the last round's evidence and the limits in section 3. If a proposal needs something from your column in section 3, I stop and list it as an open decision. I do not work around it.

## 6. Commits

- All commits stay local, on the current branch. Nothing is pushed.
- Commit messages carry no Claude attribution lines. Your CLAUDE.md rule overrides the harness reminder.
- Each round produces five commits and one tag, in the order shown above.

## 7. Morning report

- Each round's headline numbers, one line per round
- The prediction accuracy trend: hits and misses per round, and whether the predictions or the naive guess came closer
- Failures opened and closed, with F-numbers
- Any regrades, with the original and regraded numbers side by side
- Total spend against the caps
- Why I stopped
- Open decisions that need you
- The rerun command and the latest tag

## 8. What I need from you before you go

Confirm or change the caps in section 1. Nothing else is needed.
